q: Heat is the amount of energy transferred from one object to another because of a difference in ____.
e: Heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference. Heat is the amount of energy transferred from one object to another because of a difference in temperature.

q: As heat is a form of energy, heat can be measured in energy ____.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. As heat is a form of energy, heat can be measured in energy unit.

q: The unit of heat is joule (J) in ____ unit.
e: Heat is energy, so the SI unit is the joule. The unit of heat is joule (J) in SI unit.

q: Other heat units are calorie (cal) in the ____ system and kilocalorie (kcal) in the MKS system.
e: One kilocalorie raises 1 kg of water by 1 K. That is the MKS heat unit. Other heat units are calorie (cal) in the CGS system and kilocalorie (kcal) in the MKS system.

q: The heat unit in British system is the ____.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. The heat unit in British system is the British thermal unit(Btu).

q: Heat required to change the temperature of 1 kilogram mass of water by 1kelvin is called 1 ____.
e: One kilocalorie raises 1 kg of water by 1 K. That is the MKS heat unit. Heat required to change the temperature of 1 kilogram mass of water by 1kelvin is called 1 kilocalorie.

q: The German doctor, ____, found first that the energy which represents 1 cal is 4.184 J.
e: Mayer's mechanical equivalent of heat is 1 cal = 4.184 J. The German doctor, Robert Mayer, found first that the energy which represents 1 cal is 4.184 J. Robert mayer is what this sentence is naming. Stay with the quantity named in this sentence.

q: The relations between heat units are 1 kcal = ____.
e: 1 kcal = 4184 J, 1 Btu = 1055 J, and 1 ft-lb = 1.356 J. The relations between heat units are 1 kcal = 4184J. 4184j is what this sentence is naming.

q: The relation between British thermal unit and joule is 1 Btu = ____ J.
e: The British heat unit is the Btu. The relation between British thermal unit and joule is 1 Btu = 1055 J.

q: The relation between foot-pound and joule is 1 ft-lb = ____ J.
e: 1 kcal = 4184 J, 1 Btu = 1055 J, and 1 ft-lb = 1.356 J. The relation between foot-pound and joule is 1 ft-lb = 1.356 J. 1.356 is what this sentence is naming. Stay with the quantity named in this sentence.

q: The internal energy of a body is the sum of the total kinetic energy and ____ of the molecules.
e: Kinetic energy is ½mv². It is the energy of motion. The internal energy of a body is the sum of the total kinetic energy and potential energy of the molecules.

q: The kinetic energy of molecules is energy due to their ____.
e: Kinetic energy is ½mv². It is the energy of motion. The kinetic energy of molecules is energy due to their motions.

q: The kinetic energy is directly related to ____.
e: Kinetic energy is ½mv². It is the energy of motion. The kinetic energy is directly related to temperature.

q: The rise in temperature of a substance is due to an increase in the average ____ of the molecules.
e: A temperature rise means the molecules' average kinetic energy has gone up. The rise in temperature of a substance is due to an increase in the average kinetic energy of the molecules.

q: The potential energy is energy due to ____ between the molecules.
e: Internal energy is the molecules' kinetic energy plus the potential energy from their spacing. The potential energy is energy due to inter-molecular forces between the molecules.

q: The magnitude of potential energy stored depends on the ____ between the molecules (or) the particles in that substance.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The magnitude of potential energy stored depends on the distance between the molecules (or) the particles in that substance.

q: The internal energy of the substance is known as its ____.
e: Internal energy is the molecules' kinetic energy plus the potential energy from their spacing. The internal energy of the substance is known as its thermal energy.

q: The transfer of thermal energy from one substance to another is referred to as ____.
e: The transfer of thermal energy from one substance to another is referred to as heat. Heat is what this statement is using.

q: The amount of thermal energy required to change the temperature of an object by one degree is called the ____ (or) heat capacity of the object.
e: Heat capacity is the heat to raise the whole sample by 1 K, C = Q/Δθ. The amount of thermal energy required to change the temperature of an object by one degree is called the thermal capacity (or) heat capacity of the object.

q: The thermal capacity of an object is given by the formula $C =$ ____.
e: The thermal capacity of an object is given by the formula C = (ΔQ)/(ΔT). Leave the relation as (ΔQ)/(ΔT).

q: In SI unit, the unit of thermal capacity is ____ ($J K^{-1}$).
e: In SI unit, the unit of thermal capacity is joule per kelvin (J K^-1). The unit written here is joule per kelvin.

q: The thermal capacity of an object depends on ____ and a type of the material it is made of.
e: The thermal capacity of an object depends on mass and a type of the material it is made of. Mass is what this statement is using.

q: Water has a relatively ____ thermal capacity.
e: Water has a relatively high thermal capacity. High is what this statement is using.

q: Because of high thermal capacity, water is used to ____ engines.
e: Because of high thermal capacity, water is used to cool engines. Cool is what this statement is using.

q: Suppose that the internal energy of ____ of a substance changes by $\Delta Q$ due to the temperature change $\Delta T$.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. Suppose that the internal energy of n moles of a substance changes by ΔQ due to the temperature change ΔT.

q: The thermal capacity for 1 mole is ____.
e: The thermal capacity for 1 mole is molar thermal capacity. Molar thermal capacity is what this statement is using.

q: SI units of the molar thermal capacity is ____ ($J mol^{-1}K^{-1}$).
e: SI units of the molar thermal capacity is joule per mole per kelvin (J mol^-1K^-1). The unit written here is joule per mole per kelvin.

q: The thermal capacity per unit mass of a substance is the ____.
e: The thermal capacity per unit mass of a substance is the specific heat capacity. The unit written here is specific heat capacity.

q: The specific heat capacity of a substance is the heat needed to change the temperature of a ____ of that substance by one degree.
e: Specific heat is the heat to raise 1 kg by 1 K. Q = mcΔθ. The specific heat capacity of a substance is the heat needed to change the temperature of a unit mass of that substance by one degree.

q: The specific heat capacity is given by the formula $c =$ ____.
e: Specific heat is the heat to raise 1 kg by 1 K. Q = mcΔθ. The specific heat capacity is given by the formula c = (C)/(m).

q: If the mass of a substance is $m$ and its specific heat capacity is $c$, the amount of heat required to raise temperature $\Delta T$ is ____.
e: Specific heat is the heat to raise 1 kg by 1 K. Q = mcΔθ. If the mass of a substance is m and its specific heat capacity is c, the amount of heat required to raise temperature ΔT is mcΔT.

q: By rewriting the equation, the amount of heat is $\Delta Q =$ ____.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. By rewriting the equation, the amount of heat is ΔQ = mcΔT.

q: $\Delta T$ is the ____ between the final and the initial temperature.
e: ΔT is the temperature difference between the final and the initial temperature. Temperature difference is what this statement is using.

q: In the SI units, the unit of the specific heat capacity is ____ ($J kg^{-1}K^{-1}$).
e: Specific heat is the heat to raise 1 kg by 1 K. Q = mcΔθ. In the SI units, the unit of the specific heat capacity is joule per kilogram per kelvin (J kg^-1K^-1).

q: The other units used for the specific heat capacity are ____ and $cal g^{-1} ^{\circ} C^{-1}$.
e: Specific heat is the heat to raise 1 kg by 1 K. Q = mcΔθ. The other units used for the specific heat capacity are kcal kg^-1 ° C^-1 and cal g^-1 ° C^-1.

q: The specific heat capacity of water is ____ $J kg^{-1}K^{-1}$.
e: Specific heat is the heat to raise 1 kg by 1 K. Q = mcΔθ. The specific heat capacity of water is 4184 J kg^-1K^-1.

q: The specific heat capacity of ice (-10 $^{\circ}$C to 0 $^{\circ}$C) is ____ $J kg^{-1}K^{-1}$.
e: Specific heat is the heat to raise 1 kg by 1 K. Q = mcΔθ. The specific heat capacity of ice (-10 °C to 0 °C) is 2089 J kg^-1K^-1.

q: The specific heat capacity of steam (100 $^{\circ}$C to 200 $^{\circ}$C) is ____ $J kg^{-1}K^{-1}$.
e: Specific heat is the heat to raise 1 kg by 1 K. Q = mcΔθ. The specific heat capacity of steam (100 °C to 200 °C) is 1963 J kg^-1K^-1.

q: The specific heat capacity of hydrogen (gas) is ____ $J kg^{-1}K^{-1}$.
e: Specific heat is the heat to raise 1 kg by 1 K. Q = mcΔθ. The specific heat capacity of hydrogen (gas) is 14250 J kg^-1K^-1.

q: The specific heat capacity of helium (gas) is ____ $J kg^{-1}K^{-1}$.
e: Specific heat is the heat to raise 1 kg by 1 K. Q = mcΔθ. The specific heat capacity of helium (gas) is 5180 J kg^-1K^-1.

q: When heat is transferred from one object to another object the total heat lost by one object is equal to the ____ by the other object.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. When heat is transferred from one object to another object the total heat lost by one object is equal to the total heat gained by the other object.

q: According to the law of heat exchange, $\Delta Q_{lost} =$ ____.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. According to the law of heat exchange, ΔQlost = ΔQgained.

q: Since heat is a form of energy, the law of heat exchange is one particular statement of the law of ____.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. Since heat is a form of energy, the law of heat exchange is one particular statement of the law of conservation of energy.

q: The specific heat capacity of a substance can be determined using the ____.
e: Specific heat is the heat to raise 1 kg by 1 K. Q = mcΔθ. The specific heat capacity of a substance can be determined using the law of heat exchange.

q: A ____ is a device used to measure the heat flow of a chemical reaction or physical change.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. A calorimeter is a device used to measure the heat flow of a chemical reaction or physical change.

q: A calorimeter mainly consists of a metallic vessel made of ____ (or) aluminium.
e: A calorimeter measures heat by the temperature change of a known mass of water. A calorimeter mainly consists of a metallic vessel made of copper (or) aluminium.

q: The metallic vessel with a stirrer is kept in an ____ to prevent heat lost to the environment.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. The metallic vessel with a stirrer is kept in an insulating jacket to prevent heat lost to the environment.

q: There is a hole on the lid of a calorimeter through which a ____ is inserted.
e: A calorimeter measures heat by the temperature change of a known mass of water. There is a hole on the lid of a calorimeter through which a thermometer is inserted.

q: Total heat gained by the sample and calorimeter is $\Delta Q_{gained} = mc\Delta T + $ ____.
e: A calorimeter measures heat by the temperature change of a known mass of water. Total heat gained by the sample and calorimeter is ΔQgained = mcΔT + m_c c_c ΔT.

q: Most substances can exist in three states, i.e., solid, ____ and gas.
e: Most substances can exist in three states, i.e., solid, liquid and gas. Liquid is what this statement is using.

q: A transition from one of the three states (solid, liquid and gas) to another is called a ____.
e: A transition from one of the three states (solid, liquid and gas) to another is called a phase change. The name used here is phase change.

q: The change from one phase to another takes place very abruptly at a ____ temperature.
e: The change from one phase to another takes place very abruptly at a definite temperature. Definite is what this statement is using.

q: The temperature at which a phase change occurs depends on ____.
e: The temperature at which a phase change occurs depends on pressure. Pressure is what this statement is using.

q: The energy absorbed (or) liberated by a substance in a phase change is called the ____.
e: The energy absorbed (or) liberated by a substance in a phase change is called the latent heat. The name used here is latent heat.

q: The energy absorbed (or) liberated by a unit mass of substance in a phase change is called the ____.
e: The energy absorbed (or) liberated by a unit mass of substance in a phase change is called the specific latent heat. The name used here is specific latent heat.

q: If $L$ is the specific latent heat of an object, the heat needed to change the phase of that object of mass $m$ is $\Delta Q =$ ____.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. If L is the specific latent heat of an object, the heat needed to change the phase of that object of mass m is ΔQ = Lm.

q: The SI unit of specific latent heat is ____ ($J kg^{-1}$).
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. The SI unit of specific latent heat is joule per kilogram (J kg^-1).

q: It is found that the temperature ____ during phase change.
e: It is found that the temperature does not change during phase change. Does not change is what this statement is using.

q: Change from the solid phase to the gas phase is called ____.
e: Change from the solid phase to the gas phase is called sublimation. The name used here is sublimation.

q: Sublimation is used in the ____ process which does not damage food and preserves its quality and taste.
e: Sublimation is used in the freeze-drying process which does not damage food and preserves its quality and taste. Freeze-drying is what this statement is using.

q: The process of changing liquid into vapour is called ____.
e: The process of changing liquid into vapour is called vaporization. The name used here is vaporization.

q: The temperature at which a liquid vapourizes under normal pressure is called its ____.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. The temperature at which a liquid vapourizes under normal pressure is called its boiling point.

q: Heat that must be supplied to change 1 kg of liquid at its boiling point from liquid phase to vapour phase is called the ____ $L_v$ of the liquid.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. Heat that must be supplied to change 1 kg of liquid at its boiling point from liquid phase to vapour phase is called the specific latent heat of vaporization L_v of the liquid.

q: The exact value of the specific latent heat of vaporization of water is ____ $J kg^{-1}$.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. The exact value of the specific latent heat of vaporization of water is 2 255 176 J kg^-1.

q: But ____ $J kg^{-1}$ will be assumed for simplicity in calculations for the specific latent heat of vaporization of water.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. But 2.255 × 10^6 J kg^-1 will be assumed for simplicity in calculations for the specific latent heat of vaporization of water.

q: The change of vapour (or) gas phase into liquid phase is called ____.
e: The change of vapour (or) gas phase into liquid phase is called condensation. The name used here is condensation.

q: In condensation, the substance ____ heat.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. In condensation, the substance releases heat.

q: In vaporization, the substance ____ heat.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. In vaporization, the substance absorbs heat.

q: The temperature at which a solid melts under normal pressure is called the ____.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. The temperature at which a solid melts under normal pressure is called the melting point.

q: The melting point for ice under normal pressure is ____.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. The melting point for ice under normal pressure is 0° C.

q: Heat required to melt 1 kg of a solid at its melting point is called the ____ $L_f$.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. Heat required to melt 1 kg of a solid at its melting point is called the specific latent heat of fusion L_f.

q: The exact value of the specific latent heat of fusion of ice is ____ $J kg^{-1}$.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. The exact value of the specific latent heat of fusion of ice is 333 464.8 J kg^-1.

q: But ____ $J kg^{-1}$ will be assumed for simplicity in calculations for the specific latent heat of fusion of ice.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. But 3.335 × 10^5 J kg^-1 will be assumed for simplicity in calculations for the specific latent heat of fusion of ice.

q: The specific latent heat of fusion of nitrogen is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. The specific latent heat of fusion of nitrogen is 25.481 kJ kg^-1.

q: The specific latent heat of fusion of ethyl alcohol is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. The specific latent heat of fusion of ethyl alcohol is 1.042 × 10² kJ kg^-1.

q: The specific latent heat of fusion of mercury is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. The specific latent heat of fusion of mercury is 11.799 kJ kg^-1.

q: The specific latent heat of fusion of silver is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. The specific latent heat of fusion of silver is 88.282 kJ kg^-1.

q: The specific latent heat of fusion of lead is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. The specific latent heat of fusion of lead is 24.518 kJ kg^-1.

q: The specific latent heat of fusion of gold is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. The specific latent heat of fusion of gold is 64.434 kJ kg^-1.

q: The specific latent heat of vaporization of nitrogen is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. The specific latent heat of vaporization of nitrogen is 2.008 × 10² kJ kg^-1.

q: The specific latent heat of vaporization of ethyl alcohol is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. The specific latent heat of vaporization of ethyl alcohol is 8.535 × 10² kJ kg^-1.

q: The specific latent heat of vaporization of mercury is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. The specific latent heat of vaporization of mercury is 2.720 × 10² kJ kg^-1.

q: The specific latent heat of vaporization of water is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. The specific latent heat of vaporization of water is 2.255 × 10³ kJ kg^-1.

q: The specific latent heat of vaporization of silver is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. The specific latent heat of vaporization of silver is 2.335 × 10³ kJ kg^-1.

q: The specific latent heat of vaporization of lead is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. The specific latent heat of vaporization of lead is 8.70 × 10² kJ kg^-1.

q: The specific latent heat of vaporization of gold is ____ $kJ kg^{-1}$.
e: Latent heat is the heat for a change of state at constant temperature. The specific latent heat of vaporization of gold is 1.577 × 10³ kJ kg^-1.

q: The melting point and boiling point vary with ____.
e: The melting point and boiling point vary with pressure. Pressure is what this statement is using.

q: Two significant points on the pressure-temperature graph are the ____ and the critical point.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. Two significant points on the pressure-temperature graph are the triple point and the critical point.

q: At the triple point, liquid, solid and ____ phase may all exist together.
e: At the triple point, liquid, solid and vapour phase may all exist together. Vapour is what this statement is using.

q: At the critical point both the liquid and gas phases of a substance have the same ____, and are therefore indistinguishable.
e: At the critical point both the liquid and gas phases of a substance have the same density, and are therefore indistinguishable. Density is what this statement is using.

q: The melting point of ice ____ as the pressure increases.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. The melting point of ice decreases as the pressure increases.

q: For an ice skater, the pressure of ice skates ____ the melting point of ice and melts the ice under them.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. For an ice skater, the pressure of ice skates lower the melting point of ice and melts the ice under them.

q: The boiling point of water also varies with the ____.
e: The boiling point of water also varies with the atmospheric pressure. Atmospheric pressure is what this statement is using.

q: An increase in external pressure will ____ the boiling point of water.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. An increase in external pressure will raise the boiling point of water.

q: The principle that an increase in external pressure raises the boiling point of water is used in ____.
e: Fluid pressure comes from weight. A barometer reads that pressure as the height of a mercury column. The principle that an increase in external pressure raises the boiling point of water is used in pressure cookers.

q: When a pressure cooker is in operation, the pressure inside it is ____ the normal atmospheric pressure.
e: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column on a unit area. Near the ground it is about 100 kN m⁻², not 100 N m⁻². When a pressure cooker is in operation, the pressure inside it is twice the normal atmospheric pressure.

q: At twice the normal atmospheric pressure, water boils at a higher temperature of ____ and thus food can be cooked in a much shorter time.
e: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air column on a unit area. Near the ground it is about 100 kN m⁻², not 100 N m⁻². At twice the normal atmospheric pressure, water boils at a higher temperature of 120° C and thus food can be cooked in a much shorter time.

q: An object having ____ thermal capacity can be heated up easily.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. An object having lower thermal capacity can be heated up easily.

q: The temperature of mixture of water and ice will found to be ____.
e: The temperature of mixture of water and ice will found to be 0° C. 0° c is what this statement is using. 0° c is what this sentence is naming.

q: The ice is melting continuously until all the ice turns to water ____ its temperature.
e: The ice is melting continuously until all the ice turns to water without changing its temperature. Without changing is what this statement is using.
